wi_7_1_1_railroad_amphitheater.blurb: Railroad Amphitheater is a bluff-base crag on the east side of Devil's Lake, reached from the South Shore lot by following the railway line north. It is mainly traditional climbing on quartzite, with a handful of top-rope lines and a good number of boulder problems. Routes run from easy fifth class up to the low 5.12 range, with most of the grades falling in the moderate middle. Expect slab and crack climbing on sizeable lines, including a steeper, overhanging north wall and longer climbs on the south side. Access is easy and the talus runs down toward the water, so it pairs well with a swim. Bring your own gear, since the park has no bolted lines.

wi_2_qual_wall.blurb: Qual Wall is a small sandstone bluff in Governor Dodge State Park, in southwest Wisconsin, set up mostly for sport climbing. Our catalog holds about thirty lines: a dozen or so bolted routes, plus some top-rope climbs, a few trad lines and a scattering of boulder problems. Grades stretch from around 5.8 to 5.13, with the bulk of the sport routes in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, which makes it a better fit for intermediate and strong climbers than for beginners. It is unusual in a park known for bouldering. The state parks department allows roped climbing here but currently does not permit adding any more bolts, so respect the existing lines.
